/docs/get-started/.title: Get started
/docs/get-started/.description: Install smugglr, run a first sync between two SQLite files, and read what it tells you.
sections: 05 A row changed in both places

/docs/how-smugglr-decides/.title: How smugglr decides
/docs/how-smugglr-decides/.description: What smugglr compares, what it remembers, and when it stops rather than guess.
sections: 03 Changed on one side, or on both
05 It reads back what it wrote
10 How a change travels in a mesh

/docs/cli/.title: CLI reference
/docs/cli/.description: smugglr sync, mesh, stash and retrieve, their flags, the places they read and write, the config file, and the exit codes.

out.mesh_away:
$ smugglr mesh ./node.db --key-file ../mesh.key   # on rzr, restarted after being stopped longer than its graveyard (3 seconds); the scratch directory is shown as .
smugglr mesh: node rzr on UDP port 31402, key 180627566f7a4e3b
smugglr mesh: this node has been away 7 seconds, longer than the sunset (3 seconds); changes made meanwhile may not reach it. Catch up with: smugglr stash <a peer's place> <dir> --key-file <path> --node <name> --whole, then smugglr retrieve ./node.db <dir> --key-file <path> --node rzr
